summary.intent: Assess whether Phase 71 (share-invite security / IPNS data-integrity API) needed a design discussion, then run it through GSD's plan-phase pipeline to produce executable PLAN.md files.
summary.outcome: Discovered a locked D-01 decision was falsified by actual code behavior (shares are children-only, not vault-root), corrected it to an ipns_records-based ownership check, then expanded scope with the user into a full 'descriptor' terminology purge (D-10) across DB/TS/Rust plus folding D-04's CHECK into the greenfield cutover migration; planner produced 9 plans across 4 waves that passed the plan-checker (0 blockers/warnings) and, after a CONTEXT.md reformat, the decision-coverage gate (10/10).

repo: shares.rootIpnsName / share_invites.rootIpnsName always refers to a child item (subfolder/file) selected via context-menu share, never the vault root — vaults table only ever holds the top-level root (owner_id unique), so it can't authorize child-item shares

ipns_records.user_id is a 'denormalized creator marker' intentionally treated as non-authoritative (authority is the record's Ed25519 signature) — but it's the only server-side signal available for child-node ownership

readDescriptorRef/writeDescriptorRef columns contain nothing but an ECIES-wrapped key (wrapKey(itemKey, recipientPubKey)) — no extra metadata despite the entity comment claiming 'wrapped root readKey + metadata'; grant metadata (rootNodeId, rootGeneration, rootIpnsName) lives in separate columns

root_generation is a pinned snapshot at grant-issuance time, not derivable from live IPFS/IPNS metadata — it's the anti-rollback baseline consumed by both client (navigate.ts:136) and server (shares.service.ts:275-282, the phase-70.1 floor-store/high-water machinery)

writeDescriptorRef can only be minted by someone holding the parent folder's actual keys (via resolveShareWriteDescriptor) — the real access boundary is cryptographic; DB-level ownership checks are defense-in-depth only
share_invites already names its key column encrypted_key (not descriptor_ref) — inconsistent with shares table, which motivated harmonizing rename D-10

shares/share_invites schema shipped via a Phase 66 DROP+CREATE cutover migration that is still unreleased/greenfield, so renames could edit the cutover in place instead of requiring a new forward migration

GSD's decision-coverage gate parser (decisions.cjs) only recognizes '- **D-NN...**' bullet lines as decisions; rich '### D-NN — Title' heading sections parse as zero decisions (false negative), requiring a machine-readable bullet index alongside prose sections

code.finding: rootIpnsName: params.item.ipnsName — the selected item's (child node's) IPNS name, confirming shares are never vault-root scoped
server enforces forward-only rootGeneration and seeds the recipient's durable generation floor from the grant's rootGeneration; regression throws ConflictException

decision-coverage parser regex only matches '- **D-NN' bullet-style lines, ignoring '### D-NN' heading format, causing false-negative 'could not parse decisions' failures on well-formed CONTEXT.md files

workflow: When a background planner subagent halts with a finding that reinterprets a locked design decision, verify its core claim against actual code call sites before presenting it to the user — the planner in this session was correct that D-01 would break shipped subfolder sharing
A live subagent (planner) can be resumed with SendMessage carrying new decision context instead of respawning cold — preserves its prior analysis of unaffected decisions (D-02...D-09)

Background subagents can switch the shared git checkout's branch out from under the orchestrator (planner created and left HEAD on a slug-named branch) — always re-verify branch state after an agent returns before taking further git actions
GSD gate failures should be checked for parser-format false negatives (e.g., grep the validator source) before assuming a real content gap and mutating source docs to work around it

Renaming a DB column vs. renaming the corresponding TS property/API field are very different blast radii — measure with git grep counts before committing to scope; TS/API renames cross language boundaries (Rust) and require client regen
Use git grep instead of shell globs for accurate cross-repo blast-radius counts (shell glob expansion was mangled by zsh in this session)

friction: zsh glob expansion mangled an initial attempt to measure rename blast radius, requiring a fallback to git grep

GSD's plan-phase blocking decision-coverage gate returned a false negative (0 decisions parsed) against a well-formed but heading-style CONTEXT.md, requiring source investigation of decisions.cjs to fix format rather than content

Planner subagent's final report incorrectly warned about being on the wrong branch, requiring the orchestrator to reconcile git state before proceeding (turned out to be a stale-branch artifact from a background subagent switch, not a real problem)
Nyquist Dimension 8 validation gate requires a '## Validation Architecture' section only produced by RESEARCH.md, forcing a research pass even though CONTEXT.md's decisions were already exhaustive
